output.review_comment:
Requesting changes. Two of the fixes are fine: returning "<call>-All" for level scores, and raising ValueError when a player has more than 4 points and leads by more than 2 (e.g. 6–2).

Blocking: the "long deuce" branch swaps who gets the advantage when max(p1, p2) > 5. It exists only to make test_advantage_after_long_deuce pass, which expects game_score(6, 7) == "Advantage Player 1". In tennis and in the function's own docstring, the advantage goes to the player who leads by one point, which is Player 2 at 6–7. With this branch, every long-deuce advantage from 6–5 on is called for the wrong player: game_score(6, 5) returns "Advantage Player 2" and (7, 8) returns "Advantage Player 1". No test covers those cases, so the suite passes while the scoreboard is wrong.

The test looks like a typo in the spec (probably meant (7, 6), or to expect "Advantage Player 2"). The teammate asked for the tests not to be edited, so the right move was to keep the correct logic and flag the conflict to them and the match committee, not add a special case that goes against the docstring.

The PR description is also inaccurate. It says the game-over condition was changed from `>= 4 and >= 2` to `> 4 and > 2`, but that condition is unchanged and a separate check was added before it. It also presents the inversion as a real rule rather than a workaround for one test.

To merge: remove the inversion branch, keep the "-All" and ValueError changes, and raise the conflicting test with the teammate. That test will stay red until they fix it.
